sources.title: M5Stack Atom Lite official documentation PDF
facts: The document identifies SKU C008 and ESP32-PICO-D4 with 4 MB flash.
The HY2.0 custom port table assigns GPIO26 and GPIO32.
The separate bottom pin interface lists GPIO19, GPIO21, GPIO22, GPIO23, GPIO25, and GPIO33.
limitations: The download URI is mutable; the digest pins only the retrieved snapshot.
A family product document does not identify the exact physical unit or PCB revision.

sources.title: M5Stack Atomic RS485 Base official documentation PDF
facts: The document identifies SKU A131.
It describes a 6 V to 24 V input, SP3485EE level converter, and AOZ1282CI DC-DC converter.
Its base pin table labels connector pin 3 RS485_RX and connector pin 5 RS485_TX without assigning MCU GPIO numbers.
limitations: The download URI is mutable; the digest pins only the retrieved snapshot.
The document does not prove which PCB or component revision is in the selected physical unit.

sources.title: M5Stack Atom Lite simple circuit image
facts: The custom four-pin port is labeled GPIO32, GPIO26, 5V, and GND.
The bottom pad interface separately exposes GPIO22 and GPIO19 among its signals.
limitations: The immutable repository asset is a public reference, not continuity evidence from the selected unit.

sources.title: M5Stack Atomic RS485 Base schematic image
facts: The image labels U1 SP3485EN-L/TR, not SP3485EE.
Receiver output RO reaches RX through 1 kOhm, /RE is tied low, and DI is tied low.
DE is pulled up by 4.7 kOhm and pulled low through a TX-driven SS8050 transistor.
R4 is labeled 120R/NC and the terminal is labeled B, A, 12V+, and 12V-.
limitations: The asset does not identify the selected unit revision, populated R4 state, or actual component markings.
The component and voltage labels conflict with the current product document.

sources.title: M5Stack M5Unit-RS485 README
facts: The official library identifies A131 as Atomic RS485 Base.
It states that A131 does not include a built-in termination resistor and recommends external termination when topology requires it.
limitations: A software-library statement does not prove whether R4 is populated on the selected physical revision.

sources.title: M5Stack M5Unit-RS485 board-aware wiring header
facts: atomicBaseUartPins returns RX GPIO22 and TX GPIO19 for M5AtomLite and M5AtomMatrix.
The source describes A131 as connected through the Atom-family bottom base rather than generic Port A or Port C.
limitations: The mapping is strong public implementation evidence but is not a substitute for power-off continuity on the selected hardware revision.

sources.title: SP481E/SP485E datasheet linked by the A131 product page
sources.publisher: Sipex Corporation; copy hosted by M5Stack
facts: The linked file describes the 5 V SP481E/SP485E family.
limitations: Its part family does not match either SP3485EE in the product document or SP3485EN-L/TR in the schematic, so it is not accepted as the selected transceiver's electrical-limit source.

sources.title: AOZ1282CI datasheet linked by the A131 product page
sources.publisher: Alpha and Omega Semiconductor; copy hosted by M5Stack
facts: The component document specifies a 4.5 V to 36 V operating input range for AOZ1282CI.
limitations: A component limit is not the assembled A131 input rating and does not override the product document's 6 V to 24 V range.

sources.title: M5Stack Tail RS485 T002 official product documentation
facts: The page identifies Tail RS485 as SKU T002.
The Atom Lite pin table maps GPIO26 to TX and GPIO32 to RX.
The page identifies SP485EEN-L, AOZ1282CI, and a 9-24 V to 5 V conversion description.
limitations: Manufacturer family facts do not establish the selected unit revision, populated circuitry, power or GPIO-side logic levels.
No current pin assignment or power authorization follows from this source.

sources.title: M5Stack Tail485 labeled interface and power block diagram
facts: The block diagram labels B, A, 12V with a 9-24V annotation, GND, G, 5V, TXD and RXD.
It depicts SP485 and DC/DC blocks and a USB 5V-IN power path.
limitations: Despite the asset being linked under Schematics, it is not a component-level schematic.
It does not expose direction-enable topology, termination population, level conditioning or USB backfeed protection.
Graphic orientation is not measured terminal-to-wire continuity.

claims.claim: Candidate bridge UART mapping is TX GPIO26 and RX GPIO32.
GPIO26 and GPIO32 belong to the Atom Lite custom HY2.0 port, while the bottom interface exposes GPIO19 and GPIO22.
The official A131 bottom-base helper maps Atom Lite RX to GPIO22 and TX to GPIO19.

conflicts.safetyImpact: Selecting UART pins from documentation alone could observe the wrong signal or unintentionally drive an unrelated connector.
verification: Capture power-off photographs showing exact C008 and A131 SKU, PCB revision, connector orientation, and markings.
With every source disconnected, measure continuity from A131 connector RX/TX nets to Atom Lite bottom pads and identified MCU GPIO nets.
On an isolated bench, confirm MCU receive and transmit-pad behavior with a scope or logic analyzer before any field-bus connection.

claims.claim: The current product document says SP3485EE and 6 V to 24 V input.
The schematic labels SP3485EN-L/TR and marks the terminal 12V+ and 12V-.
The product page's linked transceiver datasheet is for the different 5 V SP481E/SP485E family.

conflicts.safetyImpact: The selected unit's power limits, transceiver limits, bias, termination population, and direction behavior cannot be certified from the mixed public revisions.
verification: Photograph and record the selected A131 PCB revision, U1 marking, input-terminal labels, R4 population, and connector orientation while fully de-energized.
Obtain a revision-matched manufacturer schematic and transceiver datasheet or retain the electrical facts as UNV.
Use current-limited isolated bench measurements before field power or bus attachment.

inferences.statement: For the archived schematic only, a floating or high TX leaves the SS8050 path unable to pull DE low, while the 4.7 kOhm pull-up can enable a driver whose DI is tied low. Therefore a compile-time promise not to write UART bytes is not, by itself, proof that the selected base remains passive during boot, reset, or brownout.
verification: With the revision-confirmed base isolated from the field bus and powered through a current limit, scope TX, DE when accessible, and A/B across power-on, reset, bootloader entry, UART initialization, and brownout recovery.

unverifiedGates.statement: Selected-unit SKU/revision, connector orientation and the GPIO26/32 interconnect remain unverified.
verification: Confirm capture/power/wiring context for the four private photos.
After identity and de-energization are accepted, independently review straight and crossed RX/TX-to-GPIO26/32 continuity.

unverifiedGates.statement: Exact transceiver, MCU-side logic levels, termination/bias, voltage/current limits and power backfeed behavior remain unverified.
verification: Obtain revision-matched component-level documentation or retain missing details as UNV.
Use separately approved isolated, current-limited electrical measurements after power-off identity and continuity gates.

unverifiedGates.statement: No T002-specific component-level direction circuit or boot/reset/brownout A/B passivity is established.
verification: Do not transfer A131 DE/transistor assumptions.
After scoped bench-power approval, observe the exact isolated module across power-on, reset, bootloader and recovery states before field attachment.
